title: Clone to Copy
story: If you need two copies of a book, you photocopy it. In XIOM, `.clone()` is your photocopier — it creates a deep, independent duplicate.
why: Clone is explicit and visible — you always know when expensive copies happen, unlike languages where copies are implicit and surprising.
analogy: Clone is a photocopier — you get an identical, independent copy. The original stays with you, and the copy is a separate item that can be modified independently.
try_it: Clone a Vec[Int] and add different elements to the original and the clone. Print both to confirm they're independent.
tips: Use .clone() when you genuinely need two separate copies of data
Clone is explicit — you always see it, so you always know about the cost
For cheap-to-copy types like Int, the cost is negligible; for Vec it can be expensive
Prefer borrowing (&) over cloning when you only need to read data
common_mistakes: Overusing clone() when a borrow (&) would suffice — clone is expensive for large data
Assuming clone is always cheap — for Vec[Int] of millions of elements, it copies everything
Cloning inside a loop unnecessarily — the cost multiplies
